cohort: The cohort consisted of 100 children diagnosed with Type 1 Diabetes Mellitus (cases) and 100 children without diabetes (controls).
finding: The study identified insufficient family income, low parental education, history of consanguinity, older maternal age, certain maternal health factors (abortion, infection, abnormal weight gain), hospital delivery, low birth weight, early weaning, bottle-feeding, and cesarean section delivery as significant risk factors for developing Type 1 Diabetes Mellitus in children.
mod_finding: Children born via cesarean section delivery had a higher risk of developing Type 1 Diabetes Mellitus.
birth_weight: Low birth weight was identified as a risk factor for Type 1 Diabetes Mellitus.
